title: topo_order() does not follow its own tie-break rule
statement:
Our CI cache keys are built from buildkit.graph.topo_order(), and its docstring promises a specific order: at each step, the smallest node whose dependencies have all been emitted. That is not what we get:

    >>> from buildkit.graph import topo_order
    >>> topo_order({'libcore': [], 'app': ['libcore'], 'tests': []})
    ['libcore', 'tests', 'app']     # expected ['libcore', 'app', 'tests']

Once libcore is done, both app and tests are ready, and 'app' < 'tests'. affected() returns nodes in the same wrong order; build_levels() looks fine. Please make topo_order() and everything built on it follow the documented rule for any graph, and keep cycle reporting as documented.
